notes:
- RESULT: S1, S2, the budget note and the code blocker (r-souj) are closed. I found no new allowed script that reaches Function, a host global, a built-in object, or a non-holyagent agent. No blocker. No test or gate was run (no shell), so the claim rests on reading workflow-check.ts at the worktree head.
- CLOSED S1 (built-in tampering). Every form I listed earlier now refuses. Why: a free global is accepted as a value only if it is args, undefined, NaN or Infinity (VALUE_GLOBALS, workflow-check.ts:237 and the final reference loop :801-809). So `const o = Math`, `const O = Object`, `const { assign } = Object`, `log(Math)`, `[Math]` and `Object.entries(JSON)` all fail with 'uses X as a value'. The globals can only be the direct object of a member, and memberExpression (:513-519) then allows only the names in GLOBAL_CALLS or GLOBAL_FIELDS. `assign`, `freeze`, `groupBy`, `defineProperty`, `setPrototypeOf`, `create` and every Error member are on no list. `Object.assign(Error, Object.fromEntries([['prepareStackTrace', f]]))` therefore refuses at `assign` and also at `Error` as a value. A global name cannot be declared (declare :341), so no shadow makes a global look local. A member write needs a root that holds only script-built data (memberWrites, :812-816), so `Math.max = 1`, `budget.total = 0` and `args.entries = []` refuse because the root is unbound.
- CLOSED S2 (method restriction). A listed method name must be called where it is read: `called !== CALLABLE_PROPERTIES.has(name)` refuses both `const f = xs.push` and `[1].map(xs.push)` (:521-522). The callback methods take one argument and no spread (MAX_ARGUMENTS, :224 and the check at :573-580), and Array.from takes at most two. So the thisArg route `[x].map(o.f, o)` refuses. call, apply and bind stay in DENIED_NAMES. Residual, not validated: a field with an unlisted name that holds a function can still be read into a variable or an object literal, for example `const g = result.save; const o = { push: g }; o.push(1)`. That runs g with this = o. It needs a host method on an agent result or on args. I know of no such method and I could not see the runtime, so I treat it as suspicion only. The built-ins are not reachable this way, because no static function or global object can be obtained as a value.
- CLOSED budget note. Only `budget.total`, `budget.spent()` and `budget.remaining()` pass (GLOBAL_CALLS and GLOBAL_FIELDS :201 and :217). `budget.x.y.z()`, `budget.raise(10)`, `Object.assign(budget, ...)`, `const b = budget` and `budget.total = 0` all refuse. Behavior to confirm with the maintainer: budget used as a value (the old test used `${budget}`) is now refused, so any real root script that interpolates budget will get the normal prompt. That fails closed.
- CLOSED code blocker r-souj (assign and freeze and alias forms). All eight ALLOW forms refuse: Object.assign(Math, ...), Object.freeze(JSON), `const o = Math; o.max = ...`, `const O = Object; O.assign = ...`, Object.assign(Object, ...), Object.assign(JSON, ...), `const f = Object.groupBy`, `const { assign } = Object`. The reasons are as above. The new test.each at hooks.test.ts around lines 553-623 has one case for each form.
- SUSPICION (non-blocking, no security impact found), logical assignment is treated as 'built'. In the AssignmentExpression case (workflow-check.ts:653), any operator other than `=` records the assigned value as built, `() => true`. That includes `||=`, `&&=` and `??=`, which can store the right-hand side. Allowed script: `await agent('p', { agentType: 'holyagent:reviewer-code' }); const f = async (p) => { let o; o ??= p; o.note = 'x' }; await f(args)`. It writes into a function parameter, which the rule says is refused. The impact is nil today: the parameter holds only host data (args, agent results) that the script may already write through `result.note = 'x'`, and no built-in or global object is reachable as a value. Fix for tidiness: for `||=`, `&&=` and `??=` use `builtHere(right)` like `=`.
- SUSPICION (non-blocking), a name bound by destructuring is counted as built. For example `const { toString } = {}` makes `toString` built, so `toString.x = 1` is allowed and adds a property to Object.prototype.toString, a shared built-in function. Only new properties can be added: length and name are not writable, and `constructor`, `__proto__` and `prototype` are denied as keys and properties. I found no prototype object or constructor that can be reached, so I see no exploit. Fix for tidiness: treat names bound through a pattern as unsafe.
- Also checked and sound: the agent() rules are unchanged (exactly two arguments, object-literal options, one literal agentType in the eighteen-route set, `agent` undeclarable and unaliasable). Computed access is still integer-literal only, in reads and in patterns. DENIED_NAMES still applies to properties, keys and declared names. `__proto__` and `constructor` as quoted keys refuse. `Map`/`Set`/`Error` are not constructible because `new` is refused. The lookups `MAX_ARGUMENTS[name]` and `GLOBAL_CALLS[global]` use plain objects, so an inherited key like `toString` could be found, but the only effect is that the check becomes stricter or the name is rejected earlier as undeclared. Reference resolution is lazy and real-scope, so var and function hoisting cannot make a global look declared, and the writes check no longer fails on hoisted names. The docs/hooks.md text now matches the code (the old 'any method of budget is free' claim is gone).
- Unverified: the Workflow runtime and sandbox are not in the repo and I did not inspect them, for example whether callbacks passed to parallel or pipeline receive an extra function argument that could start an agent under another name. That is unchanged by this repair and was not raised before. Not run: mise run verify, the hooks test file and any probe, because this agent has no shell.
